method: boundary certification in three phases: (1) for each account the event touched, ask the signature history (head-first, until=event) whether anything touched it AFTER the event; (2) fetch every account; (3) RE-classify the certified set after the fetch — a certification can expire in the classify->fetch gap on a live chain, and expired rows are counted, never witnessed. Only rows still certified at fetch time are witnessed against the event's own postBalances/postTokenBalances

offlist_guard.note: HARNESS INVARIANT (not a chain measurement): the classifier refuses an address that is not in the event's own account list — without it an unrelated address would certify as if it were the event's state

limits: certification covers the interval AFTER the event only: fetch-time bytes equal the POST-event state, never the pre-event state — the pre-event half of the item stays open by construction and is not claimed

certification is a property of a moment: rows whose newer-touch re-check fires between phase 1 and phase 3 land in expired_between_phases and are excluded from every witness denominator (counted, not hidden)
a certified account fetchable at witness time only; accounts that vanished by fetch time cannot be witnessed (count them via fetch nulls, not claimed here)
getSignaturesForAddress head-first with limit 100: an account with >100 newer signatures classifies conservatively as touched_after
one endpoint, one program window, ACCOUNT_CAP-bounded — a measurement window, not a population census
no audit, no external consumer, User Zero only

verdict.text: 7/60 touched accounts have no touch after the event; fetch-time lamports agree with the event's own post-state in 4 of 4 certified accounts that still exist and were still certified at fetch time (0 certifications expired between classify and fetch and 3 certified accounts are gone already — none of them are witnessed) (token bytes 2/2; wrong-side guard: pre-side agreed only 0/3); historical read anchored at current slot in 1/1; predecessor responses carried 0 account-state payloads across 6 scans

historical_read.interpretation: context anchored elsewhere: the parameter is a FLOOR, not a time machine — past-slot question answered with current state and no error
